title: Bricked couching
subtitle: Multiple parallel laid threads held down in a staggered brick pattern
excerpt: Bricked couching fills large areas by laying parallel threads across the shape and binding them down in a brick formation, staggering each row of binding stitches so the joins never line up.
sourceNotes: Therese de Dillmont, Encyclopaedia of Needlework (1886), couching chapter. Caulfeild and Saward, Dictionary of Needlework (1882).
heroPrompt: Bricked couching filling a leaf shape on linen, rows of thread held down by staggered binding stitches, close-up, natural light.

content.text: Bricked couching lays rows of thread across a shape and binds each row down with small stitches. On the first row, binding stitches sit at regular intervals. On the second row, the binding stitches are shifted half a spacing, so they sit between the bindings of the row above. The staggered pattern gives the fill its flat, even texture.

items.label: Laid thread
items.value: Perle cotton no. 5 or 2 strands of wool

items.label: Needles
items.value: Large needle for laid thread, embroidery needle size 10 for binding

content.text: Lay the first thread across the shape. Bind it down with stitches at regular intervals of about 5 mm.
Lay the second thread parallel and immediately below, leaving a small gap. Bind it with stitches shifted 2 to 3 mm to the side of the first row's binding stitches.
Continue: odd rows bind at the same positions, even rows at the half-shift position. Fill the shape row by row.

items.symptom: Vertical lines appear in the fill
items.fix: Check that each even-numbered row's stitches sit halfway between those of the odd-numbered row.

items.cause: Too much space left between parallel laid threads.
items.fix: Pack laid threads so they sit touching or very nearly touching.

content.text: Bricked couching fills shapes in crewelwork and goldwork where flat satin would be too heavy or the shape too large. The staggered pattern also appears in Jacobean laid work as a decorative filling.
